newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-BROLIN TRANSFER STOPPED BY METAL STAPLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BROLIN TRANSFER STOPPED BY METAL STAPLE.

text.p: Sweden international Tomas Brolin said a metal staple in his foot had scuppered his chances of playing for Italy's Sampdoria.
Brolin said he had been poised to sign for Sampdoria on Tuesday when he failed a routine medical examination.
He said he had been astonished by the doctor's decision that he would have to have the staple and screws -- inserted after he broke his foot in November 1994 -- removed before he could be passed fit.
Doctors at previous clubs Parma, Leeds and Zurich had all passed him fit, he said on Wednesday.
"I met Sampdoria in Lyon (France) and negotiated. The only thing remaining was a doctor's certificate and they sent me to a doctor for an examination.

"It was a purely routine thing and the thing I was least concerned about. And then the doctor said the staple had to be taken out before he would recommend me for Sampdoria. He thought the staple would give me problems in training and games," said Brolin.
"I was in shock when I left the doctor's. I can hardly believe it would end up like this," said Brolin, who has had a stormy 18 months since leaving Parma.
He fell out with former Leeds boss Howard Wilkinson and has not been able to patch things up with new manager George Graham, who barred him from playing for FC Zurich as a loaned player.
Brolin said he did not know what to do next and needed to decide whether to have the staple removed.
"But I don't have much hope that Sampdoria will change their minds," he added, saying it would take six to eight weeks after an operation before he could play.
Brolin said it appeared unlikely that clubs would employ him after the failed medical. "It's going to be tough, word gets around."
